content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of HHI intolerance",
      "quote": "Intolerance of prior HHI therapy defined as: (i) any Grade 3 or 4 AE deemed related to HHI (ii) Or any of the following HHI-related events in patients with at least 3 months of exposure to HHI therapy (exclusive of treatment breaks): • Grade 2 muscle spasms or myalgias (iia) • Grade 2 dysgeusia or anorexia, if accompanied by ≥Grade 1 weight loss (iib) • Grade 2 nausea or diarrhea despite medical management or (iic)",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "6.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The definition of intolerance is complex and may be interpreted inconsistently across sites, leading to enrollment variability and potential amendment risk.",
      "fix": "Simplify the intolerance criteria or provide clearer examples to ensure consistent application."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ambiguous 'no better than stable disease after 9 months' criterion",
      "quote": "No better than a stable disease after 9 months on HHI therapy (exclusive of treatment breaks)",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "6.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The criterion is ambiguous because it does not specify whether stable disease must be confirmed by imaging or clinical assessment, and it may be difficult to document in patients who have had treatment breaks or changes in therapy.",
      "fix": "Clarify the assessment method and documentation required to confirm stable disease after 9 months."
    },
    {
      "title": "Potential conflict in hepatic function criteria",
      "quote": "Total bilirubin ≤3.0x upper limit of normal (ULN) (or ≤3x ULN, if liver metastases). communication with and approval from the medical monitor",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "6.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The text appears to have a formatting issue: 'communication with and approval from the medical monitor' is likely a note that should be separate, and the bilirubin threshold for liver metastases is the same as the general threshold, which may be a typo (should be higher).",
      "fix": "Review and correct the bilirubin thresholds and ensure the medical monitor approval note is clearly formatted."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing safety monitoring for immune-related adverse events",
      "quote": "Assess the safety and tolerability of cemiplimab",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "2.2 Secondary Objectives",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not explicitly mention monitoring for immune-related adverse events (irAEs) such as pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathies, which are common with anti-PD-1 agents like cemiplimab. The safety section should include specific monitoring and management guidelines.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed section on irAE monitoring, including baseline and periodic assessments for these events."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for prior radiation therapy is overly restrictive",
      "quote": "Patients in Group 2 must be deemed as not appropriate for radiation therapy. Specifically, patients must meet at least 1 of the following criteria: a. A patient previously received radiation therapy for BCC, such that further radiation therapy would exceed the threshold of acceptable cumulative dose, per the radiation oncologist.",
      "page": 41,
      "section": "6.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring a radiation oncologist consultation note for all Group 2 patients may be burdensome and delay enrollment, especially in sites without easy access to radiation oncology. This could lead to screening failures and amendments.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing the investigator to document the contraindication to radiation therapy based on medical records, with a radiation oncologist consultation only when needed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory objectives limited to Group 2 only",
      "quote": "The exploratory objectives (for Group 2 only) are to explore the pharmacodynamic effects of cemiplimab in tumor biopsies",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "2.3 Exploratory Objectives",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Restricting exploratory biomarker analyses to Group 2 may miss valuable data from Group 1 (metastatic) patients, especially since the primary endpoint is ORR in both groups. Including Group 1 could provide a more comprehensive understanding of response biomarkers.",
      "fix": "Consider expanding exploratory objectives to include Group 1 patients where feasible, or justify the restriction."
    },
    {
      "title": "Potential inconsistency in measurable disease criteria for Group 1",
      "quote": "For patients in Group 1 (metastatic BCC), RECIST version 1.1 ... generally will be used to determine ORR. Clinical response criteria may be used for patients with externally visible target lesions, if all metastatic lesions are not measurable by RECIST (such as may occur in patients with bone-only metastases).",
      "page": 34,
      "section": "4.2.1 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The allowance to use clinical response criteria for Group 1 patients with non-measurable metastatic disease may lead to heterogeneity in response assessment across patients, complicating the interpretation of the primary endpoint.",
      "fix": "Define a clear algorithm for when clinical response criteria will be used in Group 1 and ensure central review is consistent."
    },
    {
      "title": "High burden of mandatory biopsies for Group 2",
      "quote": "Group 2 only (unresectable locally advanced BCC): Patients must consent to undergo biopsies of externally visible BCC lesions at baseline, cycle 1 day 22 (±3 business days), at time of tumor progression, and at other time points that may be clinically indicated",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "6.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring multiple on-treatment biopsies, including at progression, is invasive and may deter patient enrollment and lead to high dropout rates, especially in a population with locally advanced disease.",
      "fix": "Consider making biopsies optional or reducing the number of mandatory timepoints, or allow for optional biopsy sub-study."
    }
  ]
}
